descriptionChirho: Passive sense of ritual or moral defilement: to be defiled, become polluted, or be declared unclean (Nifal and Pual stems); used of persons excluded from priestly service due to unclean genealogy (Ezra 2:62, Neh 7:64) and of land/people rendered impure (Isa 59:3, Lam 4:14, Mal 1:7,12, Zeph 3:1).
Reflexive sense of self-defilement: to make oneself ritually unclean, particularly by contact with forbidden food (Dan 1:8); the subject deliberately avoids or incurs defilement.
Active causative defilement in the Piel: to profane or desecrate someone or something, as in 'how have we defiled you?' (Mal 1:7).
Causative staining or soiling in the Hifil: to stain or soil something, used metaphorically of garments stained with blood (Isa 63:3).
